member.summary: Stub for the Domain Model that can be used to perform any end of period calculations after the treatment selection and parameter updates have been performed for all elements in the current period. This can be used to calculate any additional parameters that are needed for the next period or for reporting purposes, using the updated parameter values after treatment application. member.name: M:JCass_ModelCore.ModelObjects.Budget.CanApplyTreatment(JCass_ModelCore.Treatments.TreatmentInstance)
member.summary: Checks if a treatment can be applied in the current budget period. If the treatment relates to multiple budget categories, it checks that the total cost for each category does not exceed the budget for that category in the treatment period. If the cost in ANY budget category exceeds the budget for that category, the treatment cannot be applied. Note that default situation will be that the treatment only relates to a single budget category (default as specified in model setup), so in that default case this method will return true if the treatment cost is less than or equal to the budget for that category in the treatment period.

member.name: T:JCass_ModelCore.MonteCarlo.MarkovTransitionSimulator
member.summary:
Simulates the next state from a discrete-state Markov transition matrix.
The setup data is a square matrix supplied as a . The first column (header literally state, lowercase) holds the current-state keys (one per row). Every other column header is a next-state key. Cell values are transition probabilities expressed as fractions in [0, 1] (e.g. 0.65, not 65). Blank cells are treated as 0. Each row's probabilities must sum to 1.0 (checked to four decimal places). The set of row keys and the set of next-state column headers must be identical (square + consistent).
Two sampling modes are available:
— homogeneous. Every element in the same current state draws from the identical row distribution.
— calibrated per-element. The caller supplies an already-computed per-element leave-probability p_leave_i ∈ [0, 1] and the simulator uses it directly for the stay-vs-leave draw. On "leave", the destination is sampled from the row's conditional-on-leaving distribution (excludes the stay state, renormalised). The row's baseline leave-probability p_s = 1 - p(s → s) is exposed via so the caller can construct p_leave_i (typically clamp(p_s × raw_p_i / mean_p_s, 0, 1)). Provided the caller ensures the mean of p_leave_i across the cohort in state s equals p_s, the aggregate row leave-rate is preserved in expectation.
Both overloads are allocation-free in the hot path: a couple of dictionary lookups, a small linear scan, and a returned reference to a cached column-header string.

member.name: F:JCass_ModelCore.MonteCarlo.MarkovTransitionSimulator.BaselineLeaveEpsilon
member.summary: States with a baseline leave-probability below this threshold are treated as absorbing (fully self-transitioning). No conditional-on-leaving distribution is built for them and short-circuits to a stay outcome. Uses a tolerant threshold rather than a strict zero to absorb floating-point drift from the cumulative-probability build.

The final entry of each array is forced to exactly 1.0 after the row-sum check passes, so the sampling loop is guaranteed to find a hit for any u in [0, 1).

member.name: M:JCass_ModelCore.Treatments.MCDASetup.ValidateMcdaAttributeValue(System.Double,System.String,JCass_ModelCore.Treatments.TreatmentInstance,System.Int32,System.String)
member.summary:
Asserts that a value about to be written into the MOORA attribute matrix is a finite number. Throws a support-friendly exception naming the element, treatment, attribute, and underlying source if the value is NaN or Infinity.
Why this matters: even ONE NaN or Infinity in a column causes 's Euclidean column normalisation to produce NaN for every row in that column (the existing Math.Max(1e-8, sqrt(sum)) guard does NOT handle NaN/Infinity — it only guards against an all-zero column). All treatment ranks then collapse to NaN, OrderByDescending degenerates to a stable no-op preserving insertion order, and MCDA weights are silently ignored. Failing loud here pinpoints the bad input cell before it can corrupt the ranking.

member.name: T:JCass_ModelCore.Utilities.OutputStamper
member.summary:
Provides deterministic, cross-run stable fingerprints (“stamps”) for model outputs.
Why this class exists: - .NET’s and string.GetHashCode() are randomised per process, meaning they produce different values across runs, rebuilds, and machines. - Floating-point operations can differ slightly across CPUs/JIT runtimes, leading to false “changes detected” when hashing raw double bits.
What this class guarantees: - Identical model outputs (within the chosen numeric quantisation tolerance) produce identical stamps across runs, builds, and machines. - Small floating-point noise smaller than the quantisation threshold does NOT trigger false changes. - Parameter iteration order is deterministic (sorted by name). - Strings are hashed as ordinal UTF-8 bytes (not using .NET’s randomised hash). - Doubles are rounded to and then hashed using their IEEE-754 bit pattern.
Suitable for: - detecting ANY meaningful change in model output data - caching - regression detection - reproducibility checks

member.name: F:JCass_ModelCore.Utilities.OutputStamper.DoubleDecimals
member.summary: Number of decimal places to retain when quantising numeric output values. Adjust based on desired sensitivity.

member.name: M:JCass_ModelCore.Utilities.OutputStamper.GetModelOutputStamp(JCass_ModelCore.Models.ModelBase)
member.summary:
Computes a stable deterministic fingerprint (“stamp”) for all outputs in the model.
Stamp changes if: - any output value changes beyond the quantisation tolerance, - any string output changes (ordinal comparison), - parameter names change, - model dimensions change (NElements / NPeriods).
Stamp does NOT change if: - the only differences are within floating-point noise below the quantisation threshold, - .NET runtime changes its per-process hashing behaviour.
Returns a 64-bit FNV-1a hash encoded in uppercase hexadecimal.
